claims: Self-employment income does not include net earnings from self-employment when the amount is less than $400 for the taxable year

claims: The accuracy-related penalty on an underpayment is equal to 20% of the underpayment

claims: The burden of proof shifts to the IRS when the taxpayer introduces credible evidence with respect to a factual issue relevant to ascertaining the taxpayer's tax liability

claims: If a taxpayer omits from gross income an amount exceeding 25 percent of the gross income stated in the return, the tax may be assessed within 6 years after the return was filed

claims: The IRS normally has 3 years to assess additional tax after a client files their return
If a joint return is made, the IRS has an additional year to assess tax after the filing of such joint return

claims: A claim for credit or refund of an overpayment of any tax must be filed within 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever period expires later

claims: A corporation or partnership meets the gross receipts test if its average annual gross receipts for the 3-taxable-year period does not exceed $25,000,000

claims: For self-employment income tax purposes, the term 'employee' has the same meaning as when used in the Federal Insurance Contributions Act

claims: Every person liable for any tax imposed by the Internal Revenue Code must keep such records as the Secretary may prescribe

claims: Groceries and household bills are generally considered personal expenses and are not deductible as business costs

claims: For tax year 2024, taxpayers cannot claim miscellaneous itemized deductions including unreimbursed employee expenses

claims: Internal Revenue Code Section 280E disallows deductions or credits for any amount paid or incurred in carrying on the trade or business of trafficking in controlled substances, regardless of state legality

claims: Under the cash method of accounting, you must include in your gross income all items of income you actually or constructively receive during your tax year
If you receive property or services, you must include their fair market value in income
You have constructive receipt of income when an amount is credited to your account or made available to you without restriction

claims: If you don't file your return by the due date including extensions, you may have to pay a failure-to-file penalty
The failure-to-file penalty is usually 5% for each month or part of a month that a return is late

claims: The sole shareholder and president of an S corporation is considered an employee for employment tax purposes under section 3121(d)(1)

claims: Before applying the codified economic substance doctrine, a court must determine whether the doctrine is relevant to the transaction

CRP payments are not excluded from the calculation of net earnings from self-employment
A taxpayer may conduct their trade or business personally or through an agent
Activities performed by an agent can result in self-employment tax liability for the taxpayer
CRP payments are not excluded from self-employment income even if the taxpayer is not actively engaged in farming, as long as they are participating in the CRP with the intent of making a profit

verdicts.why: Case held CRP payments includible in self-employment income because taxpayer engaged in trade or business with nexus to CRP payments.
Court explicitly held CRP payments do not constitute 'rentals from real estate' under section 1402(a)(1).
Court held CRP payments not excluded from net earnings calculation by virtue of section 1402(a)(1).
Regulations cited state taxpayer may conduct trade or business personally or through agents or employees.
Court held hiring agent to perform services does not relieve taxpayer of self-employment tax liability on income received.
Court did not address whether non-farmers with profit intent avoid exclusion from self-employment income via CRP participation.

claims: A taxpayer qualifies as a real estate professional if more than one-half of the personal services performed in trades or businesses by the taxpayer during the taxable year are performed in real property trades or businesses in which the taxpayer materially participates

A real estate professional must perform more than 750 hours of services during the taxable year in real property trades or businesses in which the taxpayer materially participates to qualify as a real estate professional
If a taxpayer qualifies as a real estate professional, rental activities are not per se passive activities under section 469(c)(2)
A real estate professional must still meet the material participation requirement for each rental activity to treat the losses as nonpassive
If a taxpayer has not elected to treat all rental houses as a single activity, each house is treated as a separate activity for purposes of determining material participation
Losses from rental activities may be considered passive if the taxpayer does not materially participate in those activities

verdicts.why: 26 U.S.C. § 469(c)(7)(B)(i) states this exact requirement for real estate professional status.
26 U.S.C. § 469(c)(7)(B)(ii) requires more than 750 hours in real property trades or businesses.
T.C. Memo. 2025-128 and T.C. Memo. 2010-232 both confirm rental activities are not per se passive for real estate professionals.
T.C. Memo. 2010-232 and 2025-128 establish that real estate professionals still must satisfy material participation requirement.
26 U.S.C. § 469(c)(7)(A)(ii) provides each rental interest is separate activity unless taxpayer elects otherwise.
26 CFR 1.469-9(j) and multiple cases confirm rental losses are passive if taxpayer fails to materially participate.

claims: An S corporation can deduct rent payments made to shareholders for board meetings held at their homes if the payments meet certain criteria
Under the 14-day rule, rental income from the rental of a taxpayer's residence is not included in gross income if the residence is rented for no more than 14 days in a taxable year
An S corporation must substantiate the reasonableness of the rent paid to shareholders
If rent payments are deemed excessive or not supported by documentation, the deduction may be disallowed

verdicts.why: Sources show S corporations can deduct rent for meetings at shareholder homes when substantiated with documentation and reasonable fair market rates.
T.C. Memo 2023-105 at *4 states section 280A(g) excludes rental income if residence rented no more than 14 days annually.
T.C. Memo 2023-105 at *7 holds petitioners must establish reasonableness of rent with documentation or credible testimony.
T.C. Memo 2023-105 at *7 shows court disallowed rent deductions where documentation was insufficient and amounts excessive.

claims: A presumption that an activity is engaged in for profit arises if gross income derived from the activity exceeds deductions attributable to the activity for any 2 of 5 consecutive taxable years
The client has only one profitable year in eight years
The presumption of profit motive does not apply to the client's activity
The Tax Court considers the existence of a business plan when determining profit motive
The Tax Court considers changes in operating methods when determining profit motive
The Tax Court considers the intent to improve profitability when determining profit motive
The Tax Court has found that a long period of losses without serious consideration of discontinuing the activity may indicate a lack of profit motive
The Tax Court considers whether the taxpayer has taken calculated steps to improve profitability when determining profit motive

verdicts.why: 26 CFR 1.183-1(c)(1)(ii) states presumption arises if gross income exceeds deductions for any 2 of 5 consecutive years for non-horse activities.
Sources do not provide information about the client's specific profitable and unprofitable years.
Sources do not state whether presumption applies or does not apply to the client's activity.
T.C. Memo 2012-17 states characteristics of businesslike operation include preparation of business plan.
T.C. Memo 2012-17 states profit motive indicated when taxpayer changes operating methods with intent to improve profitability.

T.C. Memo 2013-294 concludes lack of profit motive where taxpayer continued 17 years without approaching profitability and never seriously considered discontinuing.
T.C. Memo 2010-216 states taking calculated steps in effort to actuate business model supports finding of profit objective.

claims: An officer of a corporation is generally considered an employee of that corporation for employment tax purposes
An officer who does not perform any services or performs only minor services and does not receive any remuneration is not considered an employee of the corporation

claims: The common law test for determining independent contractor status considers the degree of control exercised by the employer
The common law test for determining independent contractor status considers the permanency of the relationship
If workers perform services that are integral to the employer's business, this supports an employer-employee relationship
If workers do not work regularly but work in the course of the employer's trade or business, this may not be significant in determining their status as independent contractors

Sources state when workers' services are integral to employer's business, this supports employer-employee relationship.

claims: Proceeds from a life insurance policy received from a nonqualified employee benefit trust are generally not taxable to the recipient under section 101 of the Internal Revenue Code

claims: The IRS allows a deduction for reasonable compensation paid to employees, including corporate officers, under section 162(a)(1)
Compensation that is excessive or unreasonable may not be fully deductible

claims: The treatment of income and losses from rental activities is generally governed by the passive activity loss rules under section 469
Any rental activity is treated as a passive activity unless an exception applies

claims: Amounts paid for insurance premiums are generally deductible under section 162(a) as ordinary and necessary expenses when paid or incurred in connection with a trade or business

claims: The 90-day filing deadline in I.R.C. § 6234(a) is not jurisdictional

claims: The Eleventh Circuit concluded that the IRS satisfies section 6751(b) if a supervisor approves an initial determination of a penalty assessment before the IRS assesses those penalties

claims: Shareholders of S corporations can receive distributions from one S corporation and then contribute those assets to another S corporation to increase their basis in the latter
